video.description:
Learn to explain how to talk about caches that save time and when they go stale: Cache Hit, Cache Miss & Time to Live, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Cache Hit - A moment when the data you need is already in the cache, so no slow work is needed.
Cache Miss - A moment when the data is not in the cache, so the app must load it the slow way.
Time to Live - How long a cached item stays valid before it counts as too old.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Cache Hit, Cache Miss & Time to Live in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Cache Hit, Cache Miss, Time to Live 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Cache Hit - A moment when the data you need is already in the cache, so no slow work is needed.
한국어: Cache Hit: 필요한 데이터가 이미 캐시에 있어 느린 작업이 필요 없는 순간

Cache Miss - A moment when the data is not in the cache, so the app must load it the slow way.
한국어: Cache Miss: 데이터가 캐시에 없어 앱이 느린 방법으로 불러와야 하는 순간

Time to Live - How long a cached item stays valid before it counts as too old.
한국어: Time to Live: 캐시된 항목이 너무 오래된 것으로 취급되기 전까지 유효한 기간

landscape.hook: Can you explain Cache Hit, Cache Miss and Time to Live in English?

dialogue.title: Fast, but is it fresh?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the profile screen loads instantly now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is a cache hit. The data was already in the cache.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Like `hit` in our code, where `cache["a"]` is not nil?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. And `miss` is the opposite, a cache miss. The key `b` is not there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What happens on a cache miss?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The app loads the data the slow way, then stores it in the cache.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But my users see old names after they edit their profile.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The cache hit returns stale data. You need a time to live.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, sixty seconds. After that, the item is too old, so it counts as a cache miss.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the time to live keeps the cache fresh.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. A cache hit is only good if the data is still valid.

dialogue.code:
import Foundation
let ttl: TimeInterval = 60
var cache: [String: (Int, Date)] = [:]
cache["a"] = (1, Date())
let hit = cache["a"] != nil
let miss = cache["b"] == nil
